name: create-at-occupied-storage-target
description: A `create` whose identity no element declares, but whose plain file name — the one composed from the identity — another element's file already holds. The store keeps every name: the new element is written to the nearest free collision-suffixed file and the element that held the plain name is left byte-identical. Nothing in the exchange shows it, and that is the contract: the response of this create is the response of a create that took no suffix, because a file name is storage and storage never crosses the boundary in either direction. A collision of FILE names is never refused: on a case-insensitive filesystem that would make `UInt16` unrepresentable beside `uint16`.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model plus one hand-authored file, `data_types/implementation/Speed_kph.yaml`, whose declared name is `VehicleSpeed_kph`. No element of the `implementation_types` layer is named `Speed_kph`, so the identity is free while its plain file name is held. The commit writes `data_types/implementation/Speed_kph~1.yaml` declaring `Speed_kph`; the change set's writer entry in the audit log records that target beside the address `{implementation_types, Speed_kph}`, and the response carries neither the file nor the suffix.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the requested address exactly. A scope is keyed by address and never by file, so the file the store chooses needs no approval of its own — it is not something the host is shown or could be shown.

input.intent: Add a shorter-named value type for the vehicle speed.

value.name: Speed_kph
value.description: Vehicle speed in kilometres per hour

after.name: Speed_kph
after.description: Vehicle speed in kilometres per hour

expected.notes: `committed`, and not a safety act: a new value type makes no check refuse less. The delta is exactly the one `create-data-type-alias.json` would produce for this payload against a model where nothing holds the name, which is the point — which file an element lives in is a fact of the store and of the audit log's written-target record, never of the protocol. An identity already declared by an element is still an `identity-conflict` (`negative/identity-conflict-duplicate-data-type.json`): what collides is an identity, never a file name.
